name: Saleor
title: Saleor SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on Saleor’s GraphQL API: setup, env and Saleor settings. 28 of 43 services wired, but cart, checkout and sign-in are not: it cannot sell yet.
lede: The Saleor connector talks to Saleor’s GraphQL API from a single environment variable. Its guide describes cart, checkout and sign-in as Saleor-native, but the coverage script counts none of the three as wired, so for now it cannot sell.
verdict: Cannot sell yet. The coverage script counts cart, checkout and sign-in as not wired — along with orders, categories, coupons, search, addresses, pages and payment methods — and CONNECTORS.md says this connector predates the current wiring pass. Its own guide adds that the card gateways throw “not implemented”.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your Saleor GraphQL endpoint

quickStartNote: The guide removes only `@misiki/litekart-connector`. A fresh clone’s `package.json` also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector`, and with two connectors installed and neither of them Litekart’s, the build stops and asks for `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR` — so this removes both.

env.name: PUBLIC_SALEOR_API_URL
env.note: The full Saleor GraphQL endpoint, such as `https://your-store.saleor.cloud/graphql/` — the endpoint, not just the host.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/saleor-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: The Litekart trio is not used in Saleor mode; `/health` reports ready when `PUBLIC_SALEOR_API_URL` is set and the Saleor connector is active.
backendSettings: Turn off email confirmation for user registration.
Allow unpaid orders in the order settings.
Allow unpaid orders in the channel settings too.
Allow the storefront’s origin in CORS: the browser calls `PUBLIC_SALEOR_API_URL` directly.
howItWorks: At boot, `init` in both hooks (through `src/lib/core/connectors/init.ts`) writes `PUBLIC_SALEOR_API_URL` onto the connector’s `BaseService.SALEOR_API_URL`. The server hook covers server rendering; the client hook covers the browser, which must reach the public Saleor URL in production.

By the guide’s account, cart, shipping rates, payment-method listing and cash-on-delivery checkout are Saleor-native GraphQL; categories map to Saleor categories; and the profile page delegates to Saleor’s `me` and `accountUpdate`. `checkoutComplete` requires an email on the checkout, so the static store config defaults `isEmailMandatory` to `true`.

Store identity, menus and plugin toggles are static — `default-store.json` under the default export of `kitcommerce.config.ts`. CMS pages are the connector’s own static placeholders. Any other Litekart REST path is never requested: list reads resolve empty, single-record reads and writes throw. From connector 1.0.4 the store lookup it once inherited from Litekart is answered by the connector itself.

The coverage script and the guide disagree. The script counts a service as wired only if it reaches the connector’s own HTTP layer, and it does not count auth, cart, checkout, order, category, coupon, search, address, user, page or payment-method. CONNECTORS.md names Medusa and Saleor as the next candidates for the source-verification sweep.
limitations: Sign-in (auth): not wired — the coverage script does not count it, though the guide describes email sign-in as native GraphQL.
Cart: not wired — the coverage script does not count it, though the guide describes the cart as Saleor-native.
Checkout: not wired — the coverage script does not count it, though the guide describes cash-on-delivery checkout as Saleor-native.
CMS pages: not wired — CMS-style pages show the connector’s placeholder content.
The card gateways — Razorpay, Stripe, PhonePe, PayPal, Cashfree, Affirm — throw “not implemented” in this connector.
Homepage sections other than the live product list come from the active theme’s static content — the standing rule for themes.
If the Saleor catalogue has no matching products, product grids render their empty or loading states; the pages still work.
The Conversational Shopping assistant is Litekart-only; its widget stays hidden in Saleor mode without firing requests.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “PUBLIC_SALEOR_API_URL is set, but it configures a different backend than the one this build runs on”
troubleshooting.fix: The variable is set while a different connector is installed. Install `@misiki/saleor-connector`, or remove the variable if you meant to run another backend. With more than one connector installed, set `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR='@misiki/saleor-connector'`.

troubleshooting.problem: The build stops with “Several commerce connectors are installed … Set PUBLIC_CONNECTOR to pick one”
troubleshooting.fix: More than one `@misiki/*-connector` is in `package.json` and none is Litekart’s. Uninstall the ones you do not run — a fresh clone also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector` — or set `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR='@misiki/saleor-connector'`.

troubleshooting.problem: `[saleor] no native implementation for get /api/...` in the console
troubleshooting.fix: The connector’s REST guard caught a path inherited from Litekart and answered it empty instead of requesting it. Each path is reported once. Harmless if Saleor has no such feature; if it has one, implement it in the connector’s matching service.

troubleshooting.problem: `http proxy error: api/... ECONNREFUSED` in dev
troubleshooting.fix: A Litekart REST path was requested from outside the connector, so neither its guard nor `blockRestFallbacks` saw it. Vite proxies `/api` to `PUBLIC_LITEKART_API_URL`, or to `localhost:7000`.

troubleshooting.problem: The store is called “Test”, or shows the wrong branding
troubleshooting.fix: Set identity overrides — `name`, `logo`, `favicon`, `currencyCode` and the rest — in the default export of `kitcommerce.config.ts`.

troubleshooting.problem: Sign-in or cart works in dev but not when deployed
troubleshooting.fix: Almost always CORS: allow the deployed storefront’s origin on the Saleor API.

faq.q: Can I sell on Saleor with Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Not yet. The coverage script counts cart, checkout and sign-in as not wired, CONNECTORS.md says the Saleor connector predates the current wiring pass, and its own guide says the card gateways throw “not implemented”.

faq.q: Why does the guide describe a working checkout when the table says it is not wired?
faq.a: The guide describes what the connector calls; the coverage script counts a service only when it reaches the connector’s own HTTP layer, and does not count cart, checkout or auth. CONNECTORS.md lists Saleor as a next candidate for the source-verification sweep that would settle it.

faq.q: Which Saleor settings does Svelte Commerce need?
faq.a: Email confirmation for registration turned off, `isPhoneMandatory` set to `false`, unpaid orders allowed in both the order settings and the channel settings, and the storefront’s origin allowed in CORS.
The full GraphQL endpoint, such as `https://your-store.saleor.cloud/graphql/` — not only the host. It is the one variable the Saleor connector needs.
